articles.title: What is Mistral AI? Everything to know about the OpenAI competitor
articles.subtitle: Mistral AI, which offers some open source AI models, has raised significant funding since its creation in 2023, with the ambition to “put frontier AI in the hands of everyone.”
articles.author: Anna Heim
articles.summary: Mistral AI, which offers some open source AI models, has raised significant funding since its creation in 2023, with the ambition to “put frontier AI in the hands of everyone.”
body: Following the Trump directive that led Anthropic to pull its latest AI models offline and growing calls for sovereign tech that reduces reliance on the U.S. , Mistral AI has been caught in a whirlwind of attention. But the French AI darling is often misunderstood, and the fact that it develops large language models (LLMs) has muddied the picture.

Anyone who judges Mistral by how close it is to becoming ‘the OpenAI from Europe’ is in for disappointment. Its chat and agent Vibe, formerly Le Chat , only has an ounce of ChatGPT’s brand recognition, and Claude is more popular than Mistral’s models even among founders based at Station F, Paris’ startup campus .

On the other hand, casual observers tend to miss that the French decacorn is following the Palantir playbook, with forward-deployed engineers that help governments and large corporations adopt AI and tailor it for their use cases.

This approach is also better suited for Mistral’s means. While the company is rumored to be raising some $3.5 billion at a $23.15 billion valuation , nearly doubling its current valuation, that’s still far less than U.S. frontier labs. But its revenues have also ramped up; in February, it disclosed that its annual recurring revenue was now above $400 million , up from $20 million just one year earlier, and claimed it was on track to surpass $1 billion in ARR this year.

This has helped Mistral gain a seat at the table in places like Davos, and even in rooms where tech CEOs have a hard time getting their message across, such as the French Parliament . Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch has become a public ambassador for a certain vision of AI , but he still has some evangelizing to do when it comes to explaining his own company.

In a lengthy LinkedIn post , Mensch broke down what the Paris-based company has been doing “for a living” — deploying its models and agent platform on the infrastructure of its Enterprise customers, and helping them build custom models with Forge , a platform that lets them use their own data for training.

However, misunderstandings and bigger hopes around Mistral don’t stem out of thin air. Named after a wind, the company pursues a grand vision. “We exist to make sure that everyone gets access to the best AI systems, outside of centralized control exercised by states or corporations that feel the need to control in-fine deployment of AI,” Mensch wrote.

This vision means that Mistral is looking beyond the enterprise. It also aims to keep on making big investments into research to keep up with foundational AI rivals — and Mensch’s post also covered where he thinks the company stands in that regard.

“Today, we do not yet own the best language models, but we’ve constantly reduced that gap. We have a very exciting model to come this summer – it will be open-weight, and we’re opening early access to it in July. In domains that are less compute bound, e.g. voice, vision and document processing, we have state-of-the-art solutions,” Mensch claimed.

Mistral’s upcoming model has already generated some buzz on X , where Mensch and Mistral backer Marc Andreessen have engaged with jokes and amplified memes on what we now know won’t be called “Le Chaton Fat.” That’s another sign that the world — especially “the rest of the world” — is keeping an eye out for whatever Mistral has in its bag.

The most interesting part may be happening behind the scenes. Earlier this year, Mistral acquired infrastructure startup Koyeb to further boost its plans to build “a true AI cloud. The company also announced a €4 billion investment strategy (around $4.56 billion) to build data centers in France and Sweden — and the sovereignty undertones are never very far.

“We’re building under the premise that AI technology is a commodity technology that every organization needs a secured and affordable supply of,” Mensch wrote. If you are curious to learn more, keep on reading.

paragraphTranslations: 根据特朗普的指示，Anthropic将其最新的人工智能模型下线，同时越来越多的呼声要求拥有减少对美国依赖的自主技术，Mistral AI因此受到了广泛关注。但这家法国人工智能宠儿常常被误解，它开发大型语言模型（LLMs）的事实也混淆了人们的视线。
任何将Mistral与成为‘欧洲的OpenAI’相提并论的人都会失望。它的聊天和代理Vibe，原名Le Chat，只有ChatGPT品牌认知度的一小部分，即使在位于巴黎Station F的创始人中，Claude也比Mistral的模型更受欢迎。
另一方面，随意的观察者往往会忽略这家法国十角兽公司正在遵循Palantir的剧本，通过前沿部署的工程师帮助政府和大型企业采用人工智能并为其用例量身定制。
这种方法也更适合Mistral的能力。虽然有传言称该公司正在以231.5亿美元的估值筹集约35亿美元，几乎是其当前估值的两倍，但这仍然远远低于美国的前沿实验室。但它的收入也有所增加；今年2月，它披露其年循环收入现在已超过4亿美元，比一年前仅2000万美元有所上升，并声称有望在今年ARR超过10亿美元。
这有助于Mistral在达沃斯等地获得一席之地，甚至在科技CEO难以传达信息的场合，如法国议会。Mistral首席执行官Arthur Mensch已成为某种人工智能愿景的公共大使，但在解释自己的公司时，他仍需进行一些宣传。
在一篇冗长的LinkedIn帖子中，Mensch分解了这家总部位于巴黎的公司一直在做什么——在其企业客户的基础设施上部署其模型和代理平台，并帮助他们使用Forge平台构建定制模型，该平台让他们可以使用自己的数据进行训练。
然而，对Mistral的误解和更大的期望并非无中生有。以风命名的公司追求宏伟的愿景。‘我们存在的目的是确保每个人都能接触到最好的人工智能系统，不受国家或公司控制的集中控制，这些国家或公司觉得需要控制人工智能的精细部署，’Mensch写道。
这一愿景意味着Mistral正在超越企业。它还旨在继续对研究进行大量投资，以跟上基础人工智能竞争对手的步伐——Mensch的帖子也涵盖了他认为公司在这方面的立场。
‘今天，我们还没有拥有最好的语言模型，但我们一直在缩小这一差距。我们有一个非常令人兴奋的模型即将在今年夏天推出——它将是开放权重的，我们将在7月开放早期访问。在计算需求较低的领域，例如声音、视觉和文档处理，我们拥有最先进的解决方案，’Mensch声称。
Mistral即将推出的模型已经在X上引起了一些关注，Mensch和Mistral支持者Marc Andreessen在那里进行了互动，并放大了我们现在知道不会被命名为‘Le Chaton Fat’的笑话和表情包。这也是世界——特别是‘世界其他地区’——正在关注Mistral手头有什么的另一个迹象。
最有趣的部分可能正在幕后发生。今年早些时候，Mistral收购了基础设施初创公司Koyeb，以进一步推动其构建‘真正的人工智能云’的计划。该公司还宣布了一项40亿欧元（约合45.6亿美元）的投资战略，用于在法国和瑞典建设数据中心——主权的弦外之音从未远离。
‘我们正在建设的前提是，人工智能技术是一种商品技术，每个组织都需要一个安全且负担得起的供应，’Mensch写道。如果你想了解更多，请继续阅读。

articles.title: NASA launched an emergency mission to stop the Swift Observatory from crashing to Earth
articles.subtitle: The Swift Observatory was launched in 2004, but recent solar storms have pushed its orbit lower, and it's in danger of burning up in Earth's atmosphere as soon as this year. To try and stave off its demise, NASA has enlisted Katalyst Space
articles.author: Terrence O’Brien
articles.summary: The Swift Observatory was launched in 2004, but recent solar storms have pushed its orbit lower, and it's in danger of burning up in Earth's atmosphere as soon as this year. To try and stave off its demise, NASA has enlisted Katalyst Space Technologies. The company's Link spacecraft launched Friday with the goal of intercepting […]
body: The Swift Observatory was launched in 2004, but recent solar storms have pushed its orbit lower, and it’s in danger of burning up in Earth’s atmosphere as soon as this year. To try and stave off its demise , NASA has enlisted Katalyst Space Technologies. The company’s Link spacecraft launched Friday with the goal of intercepting Swift, which has no propulsion system, and boosting its orbit back to its original position. Right now, Swift is circling at an altitude of 224 miles, and Link is aiming to raise that by about 150 miles.

Using a three-armed spacecraft to lift a satellite 150 miles higher into orbit is challenging enough, but the speed with which Katalyst pulled the mission together makes it even more impressive. NASA required the company to rush the job because Swift would be too low to save by October. $30 million and nine months later, help is on the way for the $500 million Swift.
The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory primarily studies gamma-ray bursts, which have been crucial to understanding the early days of the universe.

paragraphTranslations: 斯威夫特天文台于2004年发射升空，但最近的太阳风暴将其轨道推低，它有可能在今年就燃烧殆尽在地球大气层中。为了尽力避免它的毁灭，美国宇航局已经聘请了Katalyst Space Technologies公司。该公司的Link航天器于周五发射，目标是拦截没有推进系统的斯威夫特，并将其轨道提升回原来的位置。目前，斯威夫特在224英里的高空环绕，而Link计划将其提升大约150英里。
使用一个三臂航天器将卫星提升150英里进入轨道已经足够具有挑战性，但Katalyst公司迅速组织任务的速度使其更加令人印象深刻。美国宇航局要求公司加快工作进度，因为到10月份斯威夫特会太低而无法挽救。9个月后，耗资3000万美元，价值5亿美元的斯威夫特得到了援助。
尼尔·格瑞尔斯·斯威夫特天文台主要研究伽马射线暴，这对于理解宇宙的早期日子至关重要。

paragraphs: NASA launched an emergency mission to save the Swift Observatory from falling to Earth. The Swift Observatory, launched in 2004, is in danger of burning up in Earth's atmosphere due to recent solar storms that have lowered its orbit. NASA has enlisted Katalyst Space Technologies to intercept Swift with their Link spacecraft and boost its orbit back to its original position. The mission is challenging as it involves lifting a satellite 150 miles higher into orbit with a three-armed spacecraft.
